FAQ.md:105:Rich has no way of knowing how wide a character will be on any given terminal. This can break alignment in containers like Table and Panel, where Rich needs to know the width of the content.

class MarkdownContext:
    """Manages the console render state."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        console: Console,
        options: ConsoleOptions,
        style: Style,
        inline_code_lexer: str | None = None,
        inline_code_theme: str = "monokai",
    ) -> None:
        self.console = console
        self.options = options
        self.style_stack: StyleStack = StyleStack(style)
        self.stack: Stack[MarkdownElement] = Stack()

        self._syntax: Syntax | None = None
        if inline_code_lexer is not None:
            self._syntax = Syntax("", inline_code_lexer, theme=inline_code_theme)

    @property
    def current_style(self) -> Style:
        """Current style which is the product of all styles on the stack."""
        return self.style_stack.current

    def on_text(self, text: str, node_type: str) -> None:
        """Called when the parser visits text."""
        if node_type in {"fence", "code_inline"} and self._syntax is not None:
            highlight_text = self._syntax.highlight(text)
            highlight_text.rstrip()
            self.stack.top.on_text(
                self, Text.assemble(highlight_text, style=self.style_stack.current)
            )
        else:
            self.stack.top.on_text(self, text)

    def enter_style(self, style_name: str | Style) -> Style:
        """Enter a style context."""
        style = self.console.get_style(style_name, default="none")
        self.style_stack.push(style)
        return self.current_style

    def leave_style(self) -> Style:
        """Leave a style context."""
        style = self.style_stack.pop()
        return style

The issue is that inline code (and possibly other inline styles) is not being rendered correctly inside Markdown tables. Looking at `rich/markdown.py`, the `MarkdownContext.on_text` method handles `code_inline` tokens by using `self._syntax.highlight(text)`. However, when the current element is a `TableDataElement`, the text is appended to `self.content` via `self.stack.top.on_text(self, text)`. 

In `MarkdownContext.on_text`, if the node is `code_inline`, it calls `self.stack.top.on_text` with a `Text` object containing the highlighted code. But `TableDataElement.on_text` currently does this:
```python
    def on_text(self, context: MarkdownContext, text: TextType) -> None:
        text = Text(text) if isinstance(text, str) else text
        text.stylize(context.current_style)
        self.content.append_text(text)
```
The `text.stylize(context.current_style)` call might be overriding the syntax highlighting styles of the `Text` object passed from `on_text`. 

Wait, looking closer at `MarkdownContext.on_text`:
```python
    def on_text(self, text: str, node_type: str) -> None:
        if node_type in {"fence", "code_inline"} and self._syntax is not None:
            highlight_text = self._syntax.highlight(text)
            highlight_text.rstrip()
            self.stack.top.on_text(
                self, Text.assemble(highlight_text, style=self.style_stack.current)
            )
```
The `Text.assemble(highlight_text, style=self.style_stack.current)` call applies the current style to the highlighted text. Then `TableDataElement.on_text` calls `text.stylize(context.current_style)`, which again applies the current style.

Actually, the root cause is simpler: `TableDataElement.on_text` always calls `text.stylize(context.current_style)`. If `text` is already a `Text` object with syntax highlighting, `stylize` might be overriding those styles. 

Wait, if I look at `rich/markdown.py` again, `TableDataElement` is part of the stack. When `MarkdownContext.on_text` is called with `node_type="code_inline"`, it generates a `Text` object and calls `TableDataElement.on_text`.

Looking at `rich/markdown.py:664`, it maps tokens to elements. `code_inline` is not in `self.elements`. Instead, it's handled by the `if tag in inline_style_tags` block (lines 644-662). For `code_inline`, it enters a style context, calls `context.on_text(token.content, node_type)`, and then leaves the style context.

If the current element is `TableDataElement`, `context.on_text` will call `TableDataElement.on_text`.

The problem might be that `TableDataElement.on_text` doesn't handle `Text` objects correctly or the style application is wrong.

steps.message: The issue where inline code styles were being overwritten in Markdown tables has been fixed by modifying `TableDataElement.on_text` in `rich/markdown.py`. The previous implementation used `text.stylize(context.current_style)`, which replaced existing styles (including syntax highlighting) in `Text` objects. The fix now ensures that `stylize` is only called if the `Text` object has no existing style, preserving syntax highlighting for inline code while still applying the base style to unstyled text.
